adderall.name: Adderall (ADHD)
adderall.recommendations: ADHD medications deplete magnesium and B vitamins. Supplement with these to manage side effects and optimize focus without overstimulation.
adderall.timing_note: Take supplements 2+ hours away from medication

ssri.name: SSRIs (Antidepressants)
ssri.recommendations: SSRIs can deplete B vitamins and zinc. Omega-3 and magnesium support mood alongside medication.
ssri.timing_note: Consistent timing with meals helps stability

metformin.name: Metformin (Diabetes)
metformin.recommendations: Metformin users MUST supplement B12 and folate. Vitamin D3 and chromium support metabolic health.
metformin.timing_note: Take B12/folate separately from metformin (2+ hours)

statin.name: Statins (Cholesterol)
statin.recommendations: Statins deplete CoQ10 (critical for heart health). Always supplement with CoQ10, vitamin D3, and vitamin K2.
statin.timing_note: Take CoQ10 with meals, separate from statin if possible

ppi.name: PPIs (Acid Reflux)
ppi.recommendations: PPIs significantly impair nutrient absorption. Supplement B12, magnesium, calcium, and iron. Use probiotics to restore gut flora.
ppi.timing_note: Take all supplements 2+ hours away from PPI

blood-pressure.name: Blood Pressure Medications
blood-pressure.recommendations: BP meds deplete CoQ10 and magnesium. These supplements support cardiovascular health and medication effectiveness.
blood-pressure.timing_note: Magnesium can lower blood pressure; monitor with your doctor

birth-control.name: Birth Control Pills
birth-control.recommendations: Hormonal contraceptives deplete multiple B vitamins and minerals. B-complex, magnesium, and zinc support mood and health.
birth-control.timing_note: Take supplements with meals for better absorption

thyroid.name: Thyroid Medications
thyroid.recommendations: Thyroid meds are easily interfered with. Take on empty stomach, wait 4+ hours before supplements. Selenium and zinc optimize thyroid function.
thyroid.timing_note: CRITICAL: Take 4+ hours before/after other supplements and minerals

warfarin.name: Warfarin (Blood Thinner)
warfarin.recommendations: Blood thinners require careful supplement selection. Avoid vitamin K, which counteracts warfarin. Consult doctor before ANY supplements.
warfarin.timing_note: CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR before taking any new supplements

antibiotics.name: Antibiotics
antibiotics.recommendations: Antibiotics kill gut bacteria. Always take probiotics during and after antibiotics. Also deplete B vitamins.
antibiotics.timing_note: Take probiotics 2+ hours away from antibiotic. Continue 7+ days after

nsaid.name: NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen)
nsaid.recommendations: NSAIDs irritate the gut and can deplete iron and folate. Omega-3 and curcumin offer natural anti-inflammatory support.
nsaid.timing_note: Take with food. Omega-3 and curcumin have natural anti-inflammatory effects

antacid.name: Antacids (H2 Blockers, etc.)
antacid.recommendations: Antacids impair nutrient absorption similar to PPIs. Supplement B12, magnesium, calcium, and probiotics.
antacid.timing_note: Take supplements 2+ hours away from antacid

steroids.name: Steroids (Prednisone, etc.)
steroids.recommendations: Steroids deplete multiple minerals. Calcium and vitamin D3 critical for bone health. Zinc and probiotics support immunity.
steroids.timing_note: Long-term steroid use requires monitoring for osteoporosis

levothyroxine.name: Levothyroxine (Hypothyroidism)
levothyroxine.recommendations: Take levothyroxine on empty stomach. Selenium and zinc optimize thyroid conversion. Avoid minerals within 4 hours.
levothyroxine.timing_note: CRITICAL: Wait 4+ hours after levothyroxine before taking minerals

snri.name: SNRIs (Effexor, Cymbalta)
snri.recommendations: SNRIs affect serotonin and norepinephrine. Omega-3 and magnesium support mood. Avoid serotonergic supplements to prevent serotonin syndrome.

tricyclic.name: Tricyclic Antidepressants (Amitriptyline, Nortriptyline)
tricyclic.recommendations: Tricyclics deplete CoQ10 and B vitamins. Supplement CoQ10 and B-complex. Avoid serotonergic supplements.

benzodiazepine.name: Benzodiazepines (Xanax, Valium, Klonopin)
benzodiazepine.recommendations: Avoid sedating supplements that compound effects. Magnesium and B vitamins support nervous system health without excessive sedation.
benzodiazepine.timing_note: Do NOT combine with sedating supplements. Consult doctor before any changes

insulin.name: Insulin (Type 1/2 Diabetes)
insulin.recommendations: Magnesium and vitamin D support insulin sensitivity. Alpha-lipoic acid may improve glucose uptake. Monitor blood sugar carefully with any supplement changes.
insulin.timing_note: Monitor blood sugar closely when adding supplements that affect glucose

sulfonylurea.name: Sulfonylureas (Glipizide, Glyburide)
sulfonylurea.recommendations: These drugs increase insulin secretion. CoQ10 may be depleted. Avoid supplements that further lower blood sugar without medical supervision.
sulfonylurea.timing_note: Risk of hypoglycemia with blood-sugar-lowering supplements

doac.name: DOACs (Eliquis, Xarelto, Pradaxa)
doac.recommendations: DOACs have fewer interactions than warfarin but still require caution. Avoid supplements with blood-thinning effects.
doac.timing_note: CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR before starting any supplements

aspirin.name: Aspirin (Low-Dose/Daily)
aspirin.recommendations: Daily aspirin can deplete vitamin C, iron, and folate. Supplement these to offset. Avoid stacking with other blood-thinning supplements.
aspirin.timing_note: Take iron and vitamin C with food, separate from aspirin

ace-inhibitor.name: ACE Inhibitors (Lisinopril, Enalapril)
ace-inhibitor.recommendations: ACE inhibitors can deplete zinc and increase potassium. Supplement zinc but AVOID potassium supplements to prevent hyperkalemia.
ace-inhibitor.timing_note: AVOID potassium supplements unless directed by your doctor

arb.name: ARBs (Losartan, Valsartan)
arb.recommendations: Similar to ACE inhibitors, ARBs can raise potassium levels. Supplement zinc. Avoid extra potassium.
arb.timing_note: Avoid potassium supplements. Monitor blood pressure with magnesium

beta-blocker.name: Beta-Blockers (Metoprolol, Atenolol, Propranolol)
beta-blocker.recommendations: Beta-blockers deplete CoQ10 and melatonin. Supplement both to offset fatigue and sleep disruption side effects.
beta-blocker.timing_note: Take CoQ10 with meals. Melatonin at bedtime

diuretic.name: Diuretics (Hydrochlorothiazide, Furosemide)
diuretic.recommendations: Diuretics cause significant mineral loss. Potassium and magnesium supplementation is often critical. Monitor electrolytes regularly.
diuretic.timing_note: Take mineral supplements with food, separate from diuretic

gabapentin.name: Gabapentin/Pregabalin (Nerve Pain)
gabapentin.recommendations: Long-term use can affect bone density. Supplement calcium and vitamin D3. Avoid sedating supplements.
gabapentin.timing_note: Take magnesium and calcium 2+ hours from medication

opioid.name: Opioid Pain Medications
opioid.recommendations: Opioids cause constipation and nutrient depletion. Probiotics and magnesium support gut health. Avoid sedating supplements.
opioid.timing_note: NEVER combine with sedating supplements. Consult doctor

oral-diabetes.name: DPP-4 Inhibitors (Januvia, Tradjenta)
oral-diabetes.recommendations: Fewer depletions than metformin. Vitamin D and magnesium support metabolic health. Monitor glucose with blood-sugar-affecting supplements.
oral-diabetes.timing_note: Monitor blood sugar when adding new supplements

sleeping-pill.name: Sleep Medications (Ambien, Lunesta)
sleeping-pill.recommendations: Do not stack sedating supplements with prescription sleep aids. Magnesium and B vitamins support natural sleep pathways without dangerous interactions.

lithium.name: Lithium (Bipolar Disorder)
lithium.recommendations: Lithium has a narrow therapeutic window. Hydration and sodium intake affect levels. Omega-3 may complement mood stabilization. Always consult doctor.
lithium.timing_note: Maintain consistent hydration and sodium intake. CONSULT DOCTOR for all supplements

chemotherapy.name: Chemotherapy Drugs
chemotherapy.recommendations: CRITICAL: Do NOT take supplements during chemotherapy without oncologist approval. Antioxidants may interfere with treatment mechanism. Discuss all supplements with your care team.
chemotherapy.timing_note: ALL supplements require oncologist approval during treatment

immunosuppressant.name: Immunosuppressants (Transplant/Autoimmune)
immunosuppressant.recommendations: AVOID immune-boosting supplements as they can counteract medication. Vitamin D and calcium support bone health affected by immunosuppressants. Consult doctor for all supplements.
immunosuppressant.timing_note: NEVER take immune-stimulating supplements. Consult doctor for all changes

maoi.name: MAOIs (Phenelzine, Tranylcypromine)
maoi.recommendations: MAOIs have severe dietary and supplement restrictions. Avoid tyramine-containing products and serotonergic supplements. Risk of hypertensive crisis.
maoi.timing_note: STRICT dietary restrictions apply. Consult doctor before ANY supplement

antiepileptic.name: Antiepileptic Drugs (Phenytoin, Carbamazepine, Valproate)
antiepileptic.recommendations: Antiepileptics deplete multiple nutrients. Folate, vitamin D, and calcium supplementation is important. L-carnitine may help with valproate side effects.
antiepileptic.timing_note: Take supplements 2+ hours from medication. Monitor drug levels
